title: Aurora: the storage layer that sets it apart, and Aurora Serverless

videos.script: Aurora speaks PostgreSQL or MySQL, and your application will not notice the difference. The difference is underneath, in the storage. {{engine}} An RDS instance has a disk of its own. An Aurora cluster has one volume, shared by every instance, spread over three zones and written six times. {{six}} A write needs four of the six copies, and a read needs three. So a whole zone can go dark and the database keeps writing. {{quorum}} Because the replicas read the same volume, they are milliseconds behind instead of seconds. A failover copies nothing. It only moves a name. {{failover}} You will build a cluster in moto, with a writer and a replica, and fail it over. And you will see where moto's picture of Aurora stops, which is exactly at the storage. {{moto}} Then two ways to pay. Serverless, which bills for the capacity it had each second. And I/O-Optimized, which stops charging for every read and write. {{pay}} For each one you will find the line where it starts to win, with the price sheet and a calculation you can check. {{line}}
